Working with PowerPoint

PowerPoint works much like Word. You convert, clean and fill placeholders in the same way (see vignette("knittogether")). This article covers the differences, and the helpers knittogether provides for slides.

Most of these helpers check the output format, so the same Quarto document can still render to HTML. They’re easiest to use in a document you write in Quarto, but you can also add them to Markdown converted from Office.

Converting slides

Reading .pptx files needs Pandoc 3.8.3 or later. If you use Section Header slides, clean the Markdown with pptx_section_offset = TRUE:

clean_markdown("slides.md", pptx_section_offset = TRUE)

That keeps the section titles as top-level headings and moves each slide’s heading down a level beneath its section.

Slide templates

Quarto takes the look of your slides from a template, set with reference-doc like a Word reference document. Pandoc only supports a few slide layouts, so build a master deck with just those layouts. Put slide numbers, logos and text styles in the master rather than on individual slides.

format:
  pptx:
    reference-doc: template.pptx

Background images

pptx_section_slide() writes a heading with a background image when the output is PowerPoint, and a plain heading otherwise. It looks in bg_dir for an image named after the heading level (level1.png or 1.png) or the name you give in bg. Make the image the same size as your slides.

pptx_section_slide(level = 1, title = "Results", bg = "blue", bg_dir = "backgrounds")

To add a background to every heading of a level in some existing Markdown, use add_pptx_backgrounds_to_headers().

Columns

Put pptx_col_start(), pptx_col_break() and pptx_col_end() around content to split a slide into two columns. width is each column’s share of the slide, in per cent. In a Quarto document:

`r knittogether::pptx_col_start(width = 40)`

```{r}
plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)
```

`r knittogether::pptx_col_break(width = 60)`

```{r}
head(mtcars)
```

`r knittogether::pptx_col_end()`

In HTML output the columns are left out and the content runs down the page as normal.

Slide breaks

Every level 1 (#) and level 2 (##) heading starts a new slide, and everything up to the next heading goes on that slide. Unlike HTML slides, PowerPoint won’t shrink text to fit. The only way to make text smaller is to change the template, which affects every slide. Long sections need breaking up.

  • slide_break() adds a break where you put it. In converted Markdown you can type `r knittogether::slide_break()` at the right spot.
  • auto_slide_break() takes a block of text and breaks it into slides of no more than limit characters (800 by default). It breaks at a sub-heading, the end of a sentence or a paragraph where it can.

Both do nothing in HTML output. Expect some trial and error before everything fits.

Citations

Zotero’s Word plugin doesn’t work in PowerPoint, so citations there have to be typed by hand. Add the references to a Zotero collection, copy each one’s citation key, and type it into the slide as [@citekey]. If the keys match your .bib file, they come through to Markdown and the rendered output as ordinary citations. Often it’s simpler to add citations in R instead. See vignette("citations") for the bibliography set-up.
